page: Vultr vc2-16c-64gb is a Cloud Compute virtual server featuring 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon cores on the x86_64 architecture. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is provided via a local 1280 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz and includes 16 MB of L3 cache, with support for hardware-level features such as AVX, AVX-512, and AES cryptography.

Benchmark results place the server's processing capabilities in the average tier for its resource class. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test yielded a score of 21535.52, while the single-core performance reached 1451.59. Memory bandwidth tests showed 107.12 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 53.71 GB/sec for large-block writes. However, single-threaded gzip compression performance is a notable bottleneck, registering in the lower 25% tier at 23.39 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached an average tier score of 66.52 GB/sec.

A primary architectural tradeoff of this instance is its shared CPU allocation model, which may introduce resource contention under sustained, high-utilization workloads. Despite this shared allocation, the server offers a high density of memory and NVMe storage relative to its hardware class, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require substantial storage capacity and memory footprint without requiring dedicated CPU cores.

This server configuration is suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and database operations. It achieved 23.04 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a static web serving throughput of 12.01 GB/sec. It is also capable of handling lightweight machine learning tasks, demonstrating an average LLM inference speed of 115.24 tokens per second for text generation using a small 135M parameter model.
